spec: Fix round 1 for T-1274: review T-1290 requested changes. fix round 1: address review T-1290 comment orchestrator/steering_policy.py:88 [high]: evaluate() reads task['read_scope'], and a missing key raises KeyError, which is caught and returned as continue/missing_input. A grep of orchestrator/*.py finds no bus task field named read_scope. spawn.py only derives it locally when it builds the packet. If real bus tasks lack the field, every evaluation returns missing_input, so no trigger ever fires in production. The fixtures in the tests pr fix round 1: address review T-1290 comment orchestrator/daemon.py:1690 [med]: The dedupe only applies while the interval is running, and shadow rows never start the interval. In shadow mode, which is the default, a row is therefore written for every running task on every tick, including plain continue rows. That floods decisions.jsonl. It also pushes older steering rows out of the 500-row window that recent() reads, so an applied active row can drop out of the window and th fix round 1: address review T-1290 comment orchestrator/daemon.py:1706 [med]: steering_tick calls harness_depth.begin_tick, which overwrites pool.harness_depth_tick. When fast_path is active it also runs promotion.collect and evaluate a second time and may send a duplicate 'active fast path refused' notification. This happens on every tick, even when steering mode is off, because the mode check happens later inside _steering_decisions. This breaks the shadow-only rule that  fix round 1: address review T-1290 comment orchestrator/steering_policy.py:47 [low]: git status --porcelain collapses a wholly untracked directory into a single entry with a trailing slash, such as 'docs/newdir/'. matches() then compares that string against scope entries. A glob or an exact file entry inside that directory will not match, so files in a new in-scope directory are counted as out of scope. Pass --untracked-files=all, or strip the trailing slash and test the directory fix round 1: address review T-1290 comment orchestrator/daemon.py:1665 [low]: Active steering does not check promotion.evaluate for steering_policy. Setting mode to active in pool.toml immediately lets the policy message workers, without the 20-shadow-row and fix-round criteria. Fast_path is gated on promotion in begin_tick. Consider the same gate for active mode, or state in the docs that the check is manual. fix round 1 rule: evaluate() derives read scope the way spawn does (reuse spawn's read-scope derivation or accept read_scope as an explicit keyword computed by the daemon from the same helper) and never reads a task field that bus tasks do not carry; add a test with a real-shaped bus task (no read_scope key) where triggers still fire. Shadow rows: write a row only when the action is not continue or the (trigger, evidence_hash) differs from the task's last row, so plain continue ticks do not flood decisions.jsonl; recent() reads only steering rows for the task, not a global 500-row window. steering_tick must not call harness_depth.begin_tick or re-run promotion.evaluate for fast_path: reuse the tick's existing harness_depth result passed in, and return early before any state change when steering mode is off. git status runs with --untracked-files=all so new in-scope directories are not counted as out of scope. Active mode is gated on promotion.evaluate('steering_policy') like fast_path (refuse to shadow with a notify when criteria are unmet), and the docs say so. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0; do not ask questions; report files changed and failures-only output.
